sections.html:
• Strategy: where to compete, what to stop doing and how to grow.
  • Operations: processes, supply chain, quality and cost.
  • Growth and new markets: pricing, international expansion and go-to-market plans.
  • Change: restructures, mergers, new systems and culture.
  • Fractional leadership: a part-time COO, CFO or CMO for a set period.

sections.h2: Independent consultant, boutique or big firm?
sections.html:
• Independent consultants bring senior experience directly, often at a lower cost than a firm.
  • Boutique firms specialise in one sector or type of problem and add a small team.
  • Large firms suit very big, multi-country programmes that need many people at once.

• Ask for case studies with measurable outcomes, and speak to references.
  • Look for credentials such as the Certified Management Consultant (CMC) designation, awarded by national institutes that belong to ICMCI.
  • Agree the problem, scope, deliverables and how success will be measured before work starts.
  • Make sure your own team learns along the way, so the change lasts.

Read how to hire a management consultant for a step-by-step guide.

Seniority, scope, duration and how much of the work is on site all matter. Consultants charge day rates, fixed project fees, retainers or, sometimes, fees linked to results. A tight brief with clear deliverables makes quotes easier to compare.

faqs.a: A senior leader, such as a CFO, COO or CMO, who works for your business part time, for example two days a week, instead of joining full time.

faqs.q: How long does a consulting project take?
faqs.a: Anything from a one-day workshop to a programme lasting many months. Agree milestones up front so you can review progress and stop if it isn’t working.

faqs.q: Should a consultant sign an NDA?
faqs.a: It’s common, especially when they’ll see financial or customer data. Your contract should also cover confidentiality, data protection and who owns the work produced.
